pr_title: caddyhttp: document that negative idle timeouts disable them
pr_body:
Since https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/pull/7913, `read_idle_timeout` and `write_idle_timeout` default to 1 minute, and there's no documented way to turn them off.

Opting out makes sense when Caddy runs behind a reverse proxy that already handles slow clients. For instance, ingress-nginx reads the whole request body before passing it on and enforces `send_timeout`. In that setup, the wrappers only add two deadline resets per write and flush on every response, and for long-lived streams they also override deadlines set by the handler (see https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/pull/8145).

A negative value already disables them: the defaults are only applied when the value is zero, and the wrappers are only installed when it's positive. The [Caddyfile docs](https://caddyserver.com/docs/caddyfile/options#timeouts) already say so, but the JSON docs didn't, and no test covered it. This PR:

- documents that behavior on `ReadIdleTimeout` and `WriteIdleTimeout`, so it's supported rather than accidental;
- adds a test checking that negative values don't install the wrappers and positive values do;
- adds a Caddyfile adapt fixture for `read_body_idle -1s` and `write_idle -1s`.

task_text:
Idle timeouts for reading and writing on the HTTP server currently default to one minute whenever they are left at zero. A negative value already turns both off. When either is negative, the server applies no idle timeout and does not reset deadlines on each write and flush. This matters when Caddy runs behind a reverse proxy that already guards against slow clients, since the extra deadline handling is redundant there and can override deadlines a handler sets for long-lived streams.

The Caddyfile documentation says that negative values disable these timeouts, but the JSON configuration documentation does not. The JSON documentation should state this behavior so users can rely on it. Negative values should keep disabling both timeouts, and positive values should keep applying them.
